intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February

experiences.name: Zermatt Ski Safari
experiences.description: Explore the legendary slopes of Zermatt with access to over 360km of groomed pistes beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Take the Gornergrat cogwheel railway to reach high-altitude runs and enjoy varied terrain suitable for all skill levels, with breathtaking panoramic views of 29 peaks over 4000m.

experiences.name: Verbier Freeride Experience
experiences.description: Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations. A certified mountain guide leads you through untracked powder fields and challenging couloirs in the Mont Fort area, offering an adrenaline-packed adventure for intermediate to advanced skiers.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour
experiences.description: Ride the cogwheel train to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the Aletsch Glacier, and enjoy stunning views of the surrounding Alpine peaks. A once-in-a-lifetime mountain experience combining culture and nature.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening
experiences.description: Warm up after a day on the slopes with a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet restaurant in Grindelwald. Enjoy locally sourced Gruyère and Emmental cheeses paired with Swiss wines and regional bread, immersing yourself in authentic Alpine culinary culture.

experiences.name: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail
experiences.description: Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos, the highest city in Europe. This full-day cross-country skiing experience takes you through pristine snow-covered forests and frozen lakes, with optional instruction from a local Nordic coach for beginners and intermediates.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich or Milan Malpensa airport, take a regional train or bus toward Poschiavo via the Bernina Express route. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Settle in, unpack, and get a good night's rest to prepare for the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport or train station (sandwiches, pretzels, or a kebab wrap for ~CHF 8-12). Alternatively, pick up snacks at a Migros or Coop convenience store en route.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express from Chur to Tirano passes through Poschiavo — a scenic and budget-friendly rail option. Book tickets in advance via SBB.ch for the best fares. The B&B is located in the quiet village of Poschiavo in the Graubünden canton. Confirm late check-in with the host before arrival.

day_by_day.morning: After a hearty B&B breakfast, take a short walk around the charming village of Poschiavo. Explore the historic Piazza Comunale, admire the Spanish-style houses, and visit the Church of San Vittore. The village is compact and walkable — a perfect gentle start to the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Diavolezza ski area (~45 min by Bernina Express train to Pontresina/Diavolezza station). Purchase a day ski pass (budget tip: check for online early-bird deals, ~CHF 55-65/day). Enjoy beginner to intermediate ski runs with stunning views of the Morteratsch Glacier and Piz Palü.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Stroll along the village streets in the crisp mountain air. Warm up with a hot chocolate or Glühwein at a local café.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — enjoy local bread, cheese, cold cuts, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich from the B&B or grab a budget mountain lunch at the Diavolezza mountain restaurant (soup + bread ~CHF 12-15). Alternatively, bring your own thermos of soup.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Croce Federale in Poschiavo — a local trattoria offering hearty Graubünden dishes like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta) and polenta for ~CHF 18-25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rent ski equipment in Poschiavo or at the Diavolezza base station to save money vs. resort rental shops. Bring your own snacks and water to avoid expensive on-mountain prices. Bernina Express day pass or regional rail ticket covers the train to Diavolezza station.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express train to St. Moritz (~40 min, ~CHF 10-12 one way). Explore the famous resort town on foot — window shop on Via Serlas, admire the frozen Lake St. Moritz, and enjoy the glamorous atmosphere without spending a fortune.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz (funicular from town center). Ski or snowboard on well-groomed intermediate runs with panoramic Engadin valley views. A half-day ski pass (afternoon) costs ~CHF 40-50, saving money vs. a full-day pass.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by train. Relax at the B&B. Optional: join other guests for conversation or play cards in the common area.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pick up a budget lunch from a Migros or Coop supermarket in St. Moritz (sandwiches, yogurt, fruit ~CHF 8-10) and eat by the frozen lake.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using groceries from the local Poschiavo shop (pasta, local cheese, cured meats ~CHF 10-12 total). Many B&Bs allow use of a small kitchen — confirm with host.

day_by_day.notes: St. Moritz is one of the world's most expensive ski resorts, but visiting on a budget is possible by using public transport, buying supermarket food, and opting for a half-day ski pass. The Bernina railway is a UNESCO World Heritage route — enjoy the scenery!

day_by_day.morning: Try snowshoeing directly from Poschiavo — rent snowshoes locally (~CHF 15-20/day) and explore the snow-covered trails around the Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo). The flat lakeside trail is easy and incredibly scenic with mountain reflections on the frozen lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue snowshoeing or switch to a self-guided winter hiking trail toward the Alp Grüm viewpoint (accessible by Bernina Express train, ~CHF 6). Alp Grüm offers breathtaking views of the Palü Glacier and the Italian Alps — one of the most dramatic viewpoints in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. Visit the local Museo di Poschiavo (small entry fee ~CHF 5) to learn about the valley's unique Italian-Swiss culture and history.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch — buy local bread, Bündner Fleisch (air-dried beef), and cheese from the village shop (~CHF 10-12). Eat with a view at Alp Grüm.
meals.dinner: Pizzeria/Trattoria Al Cervo in Poschiavo — wood-fired pizza and pasta dishes for ~CHF 15-22 per person. A local favorite with generous portions.

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoeing is one of the most budget-friendly winter activities in the Alps — no lift pass required! The Lago di Poschiavo trail is approximately 8 km round trip and suitable for all fitness levels. Dress in warm layers and waterproof boots.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Bernina Express to Pontresina (~35 min). Pontresina is a quieter, more affordable alternative to St. Moritz. Explore the village, visit the Santa Maria Chapel with its medieval frescoes, and browse the local ski shops for any gear needs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski at Lagalb ski area near Pontresina/Diavolezza — a less crowded, more affordable alternative to Corviglia. Lagalb is known for challenging off-piste terrain and stunning views. Day pass ~CHF 55. Alternatively, try cross-country skiing (Langlauf) on the Engadin valley trails — a very budget-friendly option (~CHF 15-20 for trail pass + rental).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo. Treat yourself to a relaxing evening — take a warm bath, read, or enjoy a glass of local Valposchiavo wine from the B&B or a nearby shop.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Grab a Wurst (sausage) and bread from a mountain snack hut (~CHF 8-10) or bring your own packed lunch.
meals.dinner: Osteria della Posta in Poschiavo — a cozy local osteria serving traditional Graubünden cuisine including maluns (potato dish) and venison stew for ~CHF 20-28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country skiing in the Engadin valley is world-class and significantly cheaper than downhill skiing. The Engadin Skimarathon route passes through this area — trails are perfectly groomed in February. Pontresina is also a great base for ice climbing and winter mountaineering if interested.

day_by_day.morning: Full ski day at Diavolezza — make the most of your skills developed during the week. Try the famous Diavolezza glacier run (12 km off-piste descent to Morteratsch) — one of the most spectacular ski descents in the Alps. This requires intermediate-advanced skills and ideally a guide for first-timers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Diavolezza or take a break to visit the Morteratsch Glacier on foot. The glacier trail from Morteratsch station is free and offers an awe-inspiring close-up view of the retreating glacier with historical marker posts showing its recession over decades.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo for a celebratory final full-day dinner. Explore the village one last time under the stars — the dark skies around Poschiavo offer incredible stargazing opportunities in winter.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B.
meals.lunch: Self-service mountain restaurant at Diavolezza — choose the daily special (Tagesmenü) for the best value (~CHF 16-20 including soup and main).
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your last full evening — Ristorante Croce Federale or Hotel Albrici restaurant in Poschiavo for a 2-course meal with local wine (~CHF 30-38 per person). A well-deserved treat!

day_by_day.notes: Saturday tends to be busier on the slopes — arrive at Diavolezza early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and get first tracks on the glacier. The Morteratsch Glacier walk is free and takes about 1.5 hours round trip — highly recommended even for non-skiers.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely final breakfast at the B&B. Take a slow morning walk around Poschiavo village, pick up local souvenirs — Bündner Nusstorte (nut tart), local honey, or Graubünden wine from the village shop at very reasonable prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, take one final scenic ride on the Bernina Express toward Chur or toward Tirano (Italy side) for a short cross-border excursion (~CHF 15 round trip). The Bernina Pass views in winter are absolutely stunning. Return to Poschiavo, collect luggage, and begin journey to departure airport.
day_by_day.evening: Travel to Zurich Airport or Milan Malpensa for onward flight. The train journey from Poschiavo to Zurich takes approximately 3.5-4 hours via Chur. Book tickets in advance on SBB.ch for best prices.

meals.breakfast: Included at B&B — enjoy a final Swiss breakfast.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Poschiavo before departure (~CHF 12-15) or pack snacks for the train journey.
meals.dinner: Airport or train station food — budget for ~CHF 15-20 at a station restaurant or grab a Migros/Coop meal deal.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at most Swiss B&Bs is 10:00-11:00 AM — confirm with host. Store luggage at the B&B if needed for a morning activity. The Bernina Express is a bucket-list train journey — even a short segment is worth it. Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or point-to-point tickets in advance for maximum savings on all rail travel throughout the week.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage and take a pre-booked private transfer or night train toward Poschiavo. The journey to Poschiavo via Chur and the Bernina Express route takes approximately 3–4 hours by train or 2.5 hours by car. Check in to B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama upon arrival (late check-in should be arranged in advance with the host).

meals.breakfast: N/A – In flight
meals.lunch: N/A – In flight or airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack or sandwich at Zurich Airport (Marché or Coop to Go, CHF 10–15) before boarding your transfer to Poschiavo.

day_by_day.notes: Contact B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama ahead of time to arrange a late check-in. Pre-book your airport transfer or check SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) for the last available night connections toward Chur and Tirano/Poschiavo. Pack layers as Poschiavo sits at ~1,000m elevation and February nights are cold.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely B&B breakfast at the Panorama, taking in the stunning views of the Bernina massif. After breakfast, take a short orientation walk through the charming historic village of Poschiavo — explore the Piazza Comunale, the Spanish Quarter (La Ghetta), and the Church of San Vittore. This gentle stroll helps you acclimatize to the altitude and mountain air.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Livigno Ski Resort (approximately 40 minutes by car or shuttle from Poschiavo via the Forcola di Livigno pass — check seasonal road access). Livigno offers 115km of pistes suitable for all levels and is a duty-free zone. Rent ski equipment at one of the many affordable rental shops in Livigno (CHF 30–45/day for mid-range gear) and enjoy your first afternoon on the slopes. Alternatively, if road access is limited, explore the local Diavolezza ski area accessible via the Bernina Pass (approx. 20 minutes from Poschiavo).
day_by_day.afternoon_alt: Diavolezza Glacier Ski Area (Bernina Pass, ~20 min from hotel): A spectacular glacier ski area with panoramic views of Piz Palü and Piz Bernina. Day ski pass approximately CHF 55–65.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo and enjoy a traditional Graubünden dinner at Ristorante Albrici or Osteria Salis in the village center. Try local specialties like pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with cheese and vegetables) or capuns (chard-wrapped dumplings). Warm up with a local Poschiavo craft beer or a glass of Graubünden Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Full B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — included with stay (expect fresh bread, cold cuts, cheese, jams, coffee).
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch on the slopes — try a Rösti or soup at a mid-mountain hut (CHF 18–28).
meals.dinner: Ristorante Albrici, Poschiavo — traditional Graubünden cuisine, mains CHF 22–38. Cozy alpine atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Check road conditions for the Forcola di Livigno pass in February — it may be closed due to snow. The Diavolezza alternative is highly recommended and closer. Purchase ski passes online in advance for small discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Diavolezza Glacier Ski Area. Start early to catch the first gondola up (opens ~08:30). Diavolezza offers breathtaking glacier runs and the famous Diavolezza-Lagalb traverse — a 10km off-piste glacier descent (guided only). Spend the morning on the groomed blue and red pistes with stunning views of the Bernina Group peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, attempt the Lagalb ski area on the opposite side of the Bernina Pass road (connected by shuttle). Lagalb is a more challenging, less-crowded area with excellent red and black runs. This is a great afternoon for intermediate to advanced skiers. Beginners can continue on Diavolezza's gentler slopes. End the ski day around 16:30 and take the gondola down.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening — After returning to Poschiavo, enjoy a traditional Swiss cheese fondue dinner. Head to Hotel Croce Federale or a local mountain chalet restaurant in Poschiavo that offers fondue (book ahead). Dip crusty bread into a bubbling pot of Gruyère and Vacherin cheese, paired with local white wine or kirsch. This is the quintessential alpine après-ski experience.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Diavolezza on the mountain — hearty mountain fare, try the goulash soup or Bratwurst with Rösti (CHF 20–30).
meals.dinner: Traditional Swiss Fondue Evening at a local Poschiavo restaurant — fondue set for two approximately CHF 35–50 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Diavolezza day ski pass: approximately CHF 55–65. Combined Diavolezza-Lagalb pass available. Bring sunscreen — glacier UV exposure is intense even in winter. Book fondue dinner in advance as popular spots fill up quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour — Depart early from Poschiavo by train (SBB/RhB Bernina Express direction Chur, then transfer toward Interlaken). The journey to Grindelwald or Lauterbrunnen takes approximately 3.5–4 hours by scenic train. Board the cogwheel railway from Grindelwald Terminal or Lauterbrunnen up to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and the vast Aletsch Glacier panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — visit the Snow Fun Park for tubing and snow activities, or simply soak in the extraordinary 360° alpine panorama. On the descent, stop at Kleine Scheidegg for a coffee and views of the Eiger North Face. Return by train toward Interlaken Ost and begin the journey back toward Poschiavo (or consider an overnight in Grindelwald if budget allows for flexibility).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Poschiavo by early evening (approximately 20:00–21:00 depending on connections). Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a local Poschiavo trattoria. Tonight, try Italian-influenced Poschiavo cuisine — the valley has strong Italian cultural ties.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before departure (request early breakfast from host the night before).
meals.lunch: Restaurant Crystal at Jungfraujoch — self-service mountain restaurant with hot meals and stunning glacier views (CHF 25–35). Alternatively, pack a sandwich from the B&B.
meals.dinner: Trattoria del Centro or Pizzeria in Poschiavo — pizza, pasta, or local risotto (CHF 18–28 per main).

day_by_day.notes: Jungfraujoch train ticket: approximately CHF 145–160 round trip from Grindelwald (book online in advance for savings via jungfrau.ch). The full day trip is long but absolutely worth it. Dress in very warm layers — temperatures at 3,454m can be -15°C or colder with wind chill. Check SBB timetables carefully for connections from Poschiavo.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Safari — Depart Poschiavo early by train (RhB toward Chur, then Visp, then Zermatt — approximately 3.5 hours). Arrive in Zermatt, the car-free alpine village beneath the iconic Matterhorn. Purchase a day ski pass (CHF 85–95) and begin your Zermatt Ski Safari on the legendary 360km of groomed pistes. Start with the Rothorn or Sunnegga Paradise area for stunning Matterhorn views on the morning runs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari across to the Klein Matterhorn (Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) — at 3,883m, it's the highest cable car station in the Alps. Ski the glacier runs with views into Italy. In the afternoon, explore the Riffelberg area and the famous runs back down to Zermatt village. The variety of terrain — from wide groomed blues to challenging blacks — makes Zermatt a world-class experience.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Zermatt's vibrant après-ski scene before heading back. Stop at Hennu Stall or Papperla Pub for a glühwein or local beer (CHF 8–12). Have dinner in Zermatt before the return train — try Whymper-Stube for traditional Swiss cuisine or Elsie's Bar for a cozy meal. Return to Poschiavo by late evening.

meals.breakfast: Early B&B breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Riffelhaus 1853 Restaurant on the mountain — panoramic Matterhorn views, traditional Swiss lunch (CHF 25–40).
meals.dinner: Whymper-Stube, Zermatt — classic Swiss mountain food, fondue and raclette, mains CHF 28–45. Budget-conscious option: Coop Supermarket in Zermatt for a quick meal before the train.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is car-free — take the electric taxi or walk from the train station. The Zermatt ski pass is one of the pricier in Switzerland but the experience is unmatched. Book train tickets in advance via SBB app. The return journey to Poschiavo will be approximately 3.5 hours — check last train connections carefully.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail Day — Depart Poschiavo by train toward Davos (via Chur, approximately 2.5 hours). Davos is the highest city in Europe and home to 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic/cross-country ski trails. Rent cross-country ski equipment in Davos (CHF 25–35/day) and begin gliding through the stunning Davos-Klosters valley on the Flüela or Davos Lake trails. This is a wonderful change of pace from downhill skiing — peaceful, scenic, and a great full-body workout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the Nordic trails or switch to the Davos Klosters downhill ski area (Parsenn or Jakobshorn) for a few afternoon runs if energy allows. Parsenn is one of Switzerland's largest ski areas with excellent long runs. Alternatively, explore Davos town — visit the Kirchner Museum or simply stroll the Promenade and enjoy the mountain town atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Davos before returning to Poschiavo. Try Restaurant Bündnerstube at Hotel Morosani for traditional Graubünden cuisine. Return to Poschiavo by train (approximately 2.5 hours). Spend the evening relaxing at the B&B, reviewing photos and preparing for the final day.

meals.breakfast: B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama.
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant Schatzalp, Davos — historic mountain restaurant with panoramic views, traditional Swiss lunch (CHF 22–35).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Bündnerstube, Davos — regional Graubünden specialties, mains CHF 25–40. Or try a local Davos pizzeria for a more budget-friendly option (CHF 18–25).

day_by_day.notes: Nordic ski pass for Davos trails: approximately CHF 15–20/day. Cross-country skiing is significantly more affordable than downhill and offers a unique perspective of the alpine landscape. Davos can be busy on Saturdays — arrive early for equipment rental. Check SBB for return train times to Poschiavo.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Poschiavo — enjoy a relaxed last B&B breakfast and take a scenic morning walk or snowshoe hike around the Poschiavo valley. The area around Lago di Poschiavo (Lake Poschiavo) offers beautiful flat winter walking paths with views of the surrounding peaks. Alternatively, rent snowshoes locally (CHF 15–20) and explore the forested trails above the village for a peaceful final alpine experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of B&B Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama. Board the iconic Bernina Express (RhB) — one of the world's most scenic train journeys — from Poschiavo toward Chur or St. Moritz for a final scenic alpine experience. The Bernina Express crosses the UNESCO World Heritage Bernina railway line with dramatic viaducts, glaciers, and mountain panoramas. From Chur or St. Moritz, connect onward to Zurich Airport for departure flights, or extend your stay in St. Moritz for a final luxury afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Switzerland from Zurich Airport or continue to your next destination. If your flight is the following day, consider an overnight in Zurich and explore the old town (Altstadt) for a final Swiss city experience.

meals.breakfast: Final B&B breakfast at Berninapass Poschiavo Panorama — savor the last mountain views.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local Poschiavo bakery or deli for the train journey (CHF 8–15). Alternatively, dining car on the Bernina Express (CHF 20–30).
meals.dinner: If departing from Zurich: dinner at Zeughauskeller Zurich — a historic beer hall with Swiss classics like Zürcher Geschnetzeltes (CHF 25–40). Or airport dining at Zurich Airport's many mid-range options.

day_by_day.notes: Book Bernina Express seats in advance via RhB (rhb.ch) — panoramic car seats are popular and sell out. The Bernina Express is a UNESCO World Heritage experience in itself and a perfect finale to a Swiss Alps trip. Confirm checkout time with B&B host. Allow ample time for connections to Zurich Airport — Swiss trains are punctual but mountain connections can be affected by winter weather.

Afterward, explore the charming historic village of Poschiavo on foot — stroll through the Spanish Quarter (Quartiere Spagnolo) with its colorful Italianate mansions, visit the Collegiate Church of San Vittore, and soak in the serene winter Alpine atmosphere. This gentle orientation walk sets the tone for the week ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Board the iconic Bernina Express (Rhaetian Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage route) from Poschiavo toward St. Moritz. Enjoy breathtaking panoramic views of the Bernina massif, frozen Lake Bianco, and the dramatic Morteratsch Glacier valley. Arrive in St. Moritz and explore the luxury resort town — visit the Engadin valley viewpoints, browse high-end boutiques on Via Serlas, and arrange ski equipment rental at a premium ski shop (e.g., Stöckli or Völkl flagship stores in St. Moritz).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a celebrated St. Moritz restaurant. Return to Poschiavo by private transfer or evening Bernina Express train.

meals.breakfast: Full Alpine breakfast at B&B Berninapass: fresh-baked Engadin nut tart, local honey, Poschiavo rye bread, cold cuts, soft-boiled eggs, and freshly brewed coffee.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Café do Sabi in Poschiavo or a light bite on the Bernina Express panoramic dining car.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Acla da Fans or Ecco St. Moritz (Michelin-starred) — indulge in contemporary Alpine cuisine featuring Graubünden venison, truffle risotto, and local Engadin wines.

day_by_day.notes: The Bernina Express from Poschiavo to St. Moritz takes approximately 1 hour. Book first-class panoramic seats in advance. St. Moritz is the nearest luxury ski hub to Poschiavo (~35km). Confirm ski rental reservations ahead of time for Day 3 skiing.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day skiing in the Corviglia ski area above St. Moritz — one of Switzerland's most prestigious ski resorts with 350km of pistes. Begin with a private ski instructor for a morning warm-up session on the perfectly groomed red and blue runs. Ride the Corviglia funicular from St. Moritz-Dorf up to 2,486m and enjoy sweeping views of the Engadin valley. Carve through immaculate pistes with the Piz Nair peak as your backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the Corviglia and Marguns sectors. For the adventurous, explore the Piz Nair summit runs (3,057m) for challenging black pistes and off-piste powder fields. Enjoy a mid-afternoon break at a mountain restaurant with panoramic terrace views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by private transfer. Unwind with a hot bath or sauna if available at the B&B. Enjoy a relaxed, intimate dinner in Poschiavo.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty breakfast at the B&B: porridge with Alpine berries, scrambled eggs, smoked salmon, Bircher muesli, and espresso.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant El Paradiso on Corviglia (3-star Michelin chef Reto Mathis) — legendary mountain dining with truffle pasta, lobster bisque, and Dom Pérignon by the glass on a sun-drenched terrace.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ristorante Suisse in Poschiavo — traditional Graubünden cuisine featuring pizzoccheri (buckwheat pasta with local cheese and greens), braised lamb shank, and Poschiavo craft beer or local Merlot.

day_by_day.notes: Book a private ski instructor through the St. Moritz Ski School (Skischule St. Moritz) at least 48 hours in advance. El Paradiso requires a reservation — book well ahead as it is extremely popular. Wear high-SPF sunscreen as Alpine UV at altitude is intense even in February.

day_by_day.morning: Embark on the Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Tour — depart early by private transfer or train toward Interlaken/Grindelwald (approximately 3–3.5 hours from Poschiavo via St. Moritz and Chur). Board the cogwheel train from Grindelwald Terminal up through the Eiger and Mönch to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and the vast Aletsch Glacier panorama.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — try snow tubing or a short snowshoe walk on the glacier plateau. Descend back to Grindelwald and enjoy the charming village atmosphere. Browse local artisan shops for Swiss watches, chocolates, and handcrafted souvenirs before the return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Poschiavo by private transfer. Enjoy a celebratory Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening — a traditional cheese fondue dinner at a cozy mountain chalet-style restaurant, warming up after a spectacular high-altitude day.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at the B&B: croissants, fruit, yogurt, and a thermos of coffee for the journey.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant at Jungfraujoch (3,454m) — enjoy hot Alpine soup, rösti with mountain cheese, and hot chocolate while surrounded by glaciers and snow-capped peaks.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Evening at Restaurant Steinbock in Grindelwald or upon return, a private fondue arrangement at the B&B — classic Gruyère and Vacherin fondue, raclette, charcuterie, and a bottle of Fendant (Swiss Chasselas white wine).

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch excursion is a full-day commitment — depart by 07:00 from Poschiavo. Book Jungfraujoch train tickets in advance (Good Morning Ticket for early entry is discounted and less crowded). Dress in extreme cold-weather layers — temperatures at 3,454m can reach -15°C to -25°C in February. This is one of the most iconic experiences in Switzerland — not to be missed.

day_by_day.morning: Zermatt Ski Safari — depart early by private transfer to Zermatt (approximately 3 hours from Poschiavo via Chur and Visp). Zermatt is car-free; transfer by electric taxi from Täsch. Begin your ski safari on the legendary Matterhorn Glacier Paradise, the highest ski area in the Alps at 3,883m. Explore over 360km of groomed pistes with a private mountain guide, skiing beneath the iconic pyramid of the Matterhorn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Zermatt Ski Safari — traverse the Klein Matterhorn sector and ski the famous 'Schwarzsee' runs with direct views of the Matterhorn's north face. For the adventurous, access the Italian side (Cervinia) for additional terrain. Enjoy a mid-afternoon pause at a sun terrace mountain hut.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Zermatt before returning to Poschiavo by private transfer. Alternatively, consider an overnight stay in Zermatt (upgrade option) at a luxury hotel for a more immersive experience.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the B&B or en route at a bakery in Visp/Brig.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Chez Vrony in Zermatt (Findeln hamlet, 2,000m) — one of Switzerland's most celebrated mountain restaurants. Enjoy Valais beef tartare, homemade pasta, and local Valais wines on a sun-drenched terrace with Matterhorn views.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant Zum See in Zermatt — a legendary rustic chalet restaurant accessible only on skis or by foot, serving exquisite Alpine cuisine including venison ragout, homemade spätzle, and Valais Pinot Noir.

day_by_day.notes: Zermatt is a full-day excursion from Poschiavo — an early start is essential. Book Chez Vrony and Zum See well in advance as they are among the most sought-after mountain restaurants in Switzerland. The Matterhorn Glacier Paradise cable car reaches 3,883m — altitude awareness is important. Private mountain guide booking recommended through Zermatt Mountain Guides office.

day_by_day.morning: Verbier Freeride Experience — depart by private transfer to Verbier (approximately 3.5 hours from Poschiavo). Join a guided off-piste freeride session in Verbier, one of the world's top freeride destinations and home of the legendary Freeride World Tour. Your certified IFMGA mountain guide will assess snow conditions and lead you through the iconic 'Stairway to Heaven' couloirs and the vast off-piste terrain of the Mont Fort sector (3,330m).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the freeride session in Verbier's backcountry — explore the Tortin glacier bowl and the legendary 'Vallon d'Arby' powder fields. This is world-class off-piste skiing at its finest. Return to the resort village for equipment storage and a warm-up.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Verbier before the return transfer to Poschiavo. Verbier's après-ski scene is legendary — enjoy a cocktail at the iconic Farm Club or Farinet Bar before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the B&B or a premium café in Martigny en route.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cabane du Mont Fort (3,330m) — a classic Swiss Alpine hut serving hearty mountain fare: lentil soup, cheese rösti, and hot mulled wine (Glühwein) after a morning of freeride skiing.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurant La Grange in Verbier — a sophisticated Alpine restaurant with exposed stone walls, candlelight, and a menu featuring Charolais beef fondue bourguignonne, black truffle risotto, and an extensive Swiss and French wine cellar.

day_by_day.notes: The Verbier Freeride Experience requires intermediate-to-advanced off-piste skiing ability. Avalanche safety equipment (beacon, probe, shovel) is mandatory and provided by the guide. Book the IFMGA-certified guide through Verbier's Bureau des Guides at least 1 week in advance. Snow conditions in February are typically excellent for freeride. This is a physically demanding day — rest well the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Davos Cross-Country Skiing & Nordic Trail — a more relaxed final full day. Travel by Bernina Express and Rhaetian Railway to Davos (approximately 2 hours from Poschiavo via Filisur). Glide through 100km of perfectly groomed Nordic trails around Davos, the highest city in Europe at 1,560m. Enjoy a guided classic or skate-skiing session through the pristine Landwasser valley and Flüela Pass surroundings — a serene contrast to the high-octane downhill days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Davos town — visit the Kirchner Museum (dedicated to Expressionist painter Ernst Ludwig Kirchner), browse the elegant Promenade for luxury Swiss watches and chocolates, or enjoy a relaxing treatment at one of Davos's renowned wellness spas (e.g., Intercontinental Davos Spa). Return to Poschiavo by train in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Poschiavo — a special final evening celebrating an extraordinary week in the Swiss Alps. Reflect on the week's adventures over a luxurious multi-course dinner.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the B&B: full spread of Engadin specialties — nusstorte (nut tart), local honey, Poschiavo rye bread, fresh fruit, yogurt, and a celebratory glass of Prosecco.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Bolgenschanze in Davos — a classic Swiss mountain restaurant with panoramic views, serving Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), Capuns (Swiss chard rolls with spätzle), and local Graubünden wine.
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Ristorante La Stüa in Poschiavo or a private chef dinner arranged at the B&B — a curated 5-course tasting menu featuring Valposchiavo regional specialties: chestnut soup, handmade pizzoccheri, slow-roasted Graubünden lamb, local cheese selection, and a bottle of aged Sforzato di Valtellina DOCG to toast an unforgettable Alpine adventure.

day_by_day.notes: Nordic skiing in Davos is suitable for all fitness levels and provides a wonderful active recovery after the intense downhill and freeride days. Davos cross-country ski passes and equipment rental available at the Nordic Center Davos. If departing the following morning, arrange a private luxury transfer from Poschiavo to Zurich Airport or Milan Malpensa (approximately 3 hours) — book in advance. Pack and prepare luggage this evening for an early departure if needed.
